title: Print Header Footer Navbar Spacing Parity
description: In the Zwischenbericht mit Bestand print report, the header (navbar) and footer chrome spacing no longer matches the on-screen app UI's navbar/footer spacing. The header currently has too little vertical spacing (too cramped) and the footer has way too much spacing (too much gap). Need to bring both back into parity with the app UI's navbar/footer padding, likely by adjusting headsep/footskip and/or internal chrome bar padding in print/tex/semio-window.sty (see SemioChromeNavbarHead, SemioChromeFooterHead, headsep=\semio@spacing@double, semio@chrome@footer@reserve computation around line 2621-2634).
summary:
Second follow-up: after the previous fix (navbar/footer chip-to-border gap symmetry via explicit vbox anchoring), the dev reported the header rule now cut straight through the navbar chips/icon instead of sitting cleanly below them.

Root cause: `\semio@chrome@dims@compute` (print/tex/semio-window.sty) set `\semio@chrome@row@height` (and `row@height@footer`) to just `\semio@chrome@font@chip` — the bare font size (6.57pt) — with no allowance for the chip's own padding (`\semio@chrome@padding`, 0.2em each side) and border (`\semio@stroke@hairline`, 0.75pt each side). A real navbar/footer chip (built via `\semio@chrome@chip`, an `\fcolorbox` around the text) actually measures ht+dp = 12.45pt (confirmed via `\savebox`+`\the\ht`/`\the\dp` debug instrumentation), almost exactly double the declared row height. Since `\semio@chrome@bar@threezone` centers the whole chip row inside a `\vbox to \semio@chrome@row@height{...}`, every chip row was silently overflowing that inner box by ~5.88pt — this is the exact figure behind the recurring "Overfull \vbox (5.87991pt too high)" warning seen on every page throughout this whole investigation, which I'd previously (wrongly) dismissed as an unrelated page-output artifact.

For the footer this overflow was invisible because the outer `\vbox to \semio@chrome@footer@height` (1.8em, much taller than the inner row) had enough slack to absorb it. For the navbar, the previous fix had tied `\headheight` exactly to `\semio@chrome@navbar@height + hairline` with zero slack, so the same ~5.88pt overflow had nowhere to go and bled straight through the rule that immediately follows the navbar colorbox.

Fixed by changing `row@height`/`row@height@footer` to the same font+2×padding+2×hairline formula already used for `\semio@chrome@titlebar@height` (12.45pt, matching the measured real chip extent exactly), so the inner threezone box no longer overflows in either bar. Also removed the `\savebox`/`\typeout` debug instrumentation used to diagnose this (accounted for the "nx build cache silently serves stale PDFs" trap noted in the previous close — used `--skip-nx-cache` throughout this round).

Verified via `--skip-nx-cache` rebuilds of the real mit-bestand zwischenbericht document and all print/dist templates (report, paper, flyer, forschungsbericht, zwischenbericht, kompaktbericht), rasterizing header/footer close-ups: navbar icon+chips are now visibly larger (correct — they were being under-sized as well as clipped) and sit with a clean small gap above the rule, matching the footer's gap, on both scrreprt and scrartcl templates.
